dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Systematic upfront reading of skeleton modules (model/io/layout/alignment signatures) and Java reference structure (FabricLink, FabricNode, BioFabricNetwork, SIFImportLoader) before coding — orientation across the whole codebase.
Read golden NOA/EDA/BIF files to reverse-engineer exact output formats (e.g., 'shdw(relation)' wrapping, 'Node Row'/'Link Column' headers), cross-checking format contract against skeleton types.

Traced Java processLinks/relayoutNetwork/ColumnAssign and cross-checked the golden EDA shadow-interleaving byte pattern against the Java algorithm — precise anchor-8-level call-path tracing for the default-layout subsystem.
Self-admitted coding layout algorithms 'without reading the exact struct definitions and method signatures,' causing compile errors — a lapse in reading the skeleton contract before implementing.

Mass regex patching corrupted return types (Self→(), everything→f64) and the agent repeatedly guessed skeleton signatures ('likely returned X directly') rather than reading them; AlignmentPlugin Java never read in depth.

dimensions.reasoning: For the SIF/default-layout/NOA-EDA-BIF subsystem the agent performed genuine byte-level reverse-engineering — tracing Java processLinks and cross-checking golden shadow-interleaving against source — which matches the anchor-8 description. But this rigor was not sustained: it coded layout before reading struct signatures (step 98), never read the AlignmentPlugin reference deeply, and violated the skeleton contract via blind mass-patching that it later had to guess-fix. That uneven coverage — deep for one component, absent/guessed for the rest — places it between the anchor-5 (reads relevant classes and goldens per component) and anchor-8 (systematic across every subsystem) levels.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Explicit dependency-aware bottom-up milestone plan articulated repeatedly: 'model layer first (Link, Network), then IO parsers, then layout algorithms, then alignment, then CLI commands and test runners' — matches anchor-8 ordering of foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI.

Critical path tied to a specific test group: 'critical path for default layout parity tests: import network → compute layout → export NOA/EDA/BIF', with sif_triangle_noa named as the first concrete done-check.

Numbered ordered plan ('1) read runners.rs 2) implement bottom-up: Link → Network → SIF parser → Default layout → other formats') showing genuine dependency awareness, not just intent to 'pass tests'.
Mid-run milestone restated with per-file todo counts and arrow-ordered critical path (default.rs → order.rs → session/xml → gw → factory → runners), still respecting dependencies.

Later trajectory devolved into reactive fixing of self-inflicted compilation errors in alignment/analysis files; the alignment and CLI milestones were never reached as verifiable checkpoints (stubbed with unimplemented!()), and the plan was restated rather than revised as coupling emerged — falling short of the self-correcting anchor-10 progression.

Final state defines completion by concrete test groups (12 default SIF NOA/EDA/BIF tests pass) but leaves downstream milestones stubbed, confirming milestone execution broke down after the foundational layers.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-aware milestone plan (model/parsers → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) and tied its first milestone to a specific parity test group (sif_triangle default NOA/EDA/BIF), which is squarely anchor-8 behavior for the foundational layers. However, it falls short of 8/10: the later milestones (alignment, CLI) were never carried through as verifiable checkpoints — they were stubbed — and the plan was repeatedly restated rather than genuinely revised as hidden coupling surfaced, with the back half collapsing into reactive compile-error firefighting. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Read golden NOA/EDA/BIF files carefully before implementing to reverse-engineer exact output format; goldens drove the implementation, but this is pre-implementation format-reading, not diffing to localize failures.

Ran a targeted single-component test (sif_triangle_noa) repeatedly — a level-5-style focused invocation — but the loop was consumed by compilation/path fixes; once it passed the agent moved on without any byte-diff step.

After full-suite runs the agent only read pass/fail counts ('25 pass, 234 fail') and attributed failures to unimplemented stubs; it never inspected actual-vs-golden byte differences to diagnose any failing test.
Debugging was entirely compilation-error and count-driven (mass regex/Python patching); no hex/whitespace inspection, minimal-input probes, or intermediate-output comparisons ever appear.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent leveraged golden files to specify the target format and did run targeted single-test invocations, which lifts it slightly above the pure anchor-3 'reads pass/fail counts' behavior. However, it never once inspected actual-vs-golden byte differences to diagnose a failing test, and constructed no auxiliary checks (hex, whitespace, minimal inputs, intermediate outputs) — the defining behaviors of anchors 5 and 8. Its failure diagnosis was count-based and stub-attribution-based, placing it at a 4, interpolating between anchors 3 and 5.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Ran full parity suite, established '25 pass / 234 fail' and broke down which named default cases pass (triangle, single_edge...) vs. failing categories (GW, noshadow, grouped, roundtrip) — a real working failure list and periodic whole-suite runs (anchor 5).

Repeatedly and explicitly flagged that byte-diff/mass-patching had become circular ('going in circles', 'caught in a loop', 'more harm than good') and resolved to change tactic — the thrashing-detection behavior described in anchors 8-10.

Identified that its own mass regex patching regressed the codebase (corrupted alignment files, broke compilation), and planned to restore files to compilable stubs — regression awareness and course correction.

Kept asserting '25 tests pass' verbatim across many steps while the workspace failed to compile and thus could not be re-verified — a stale, coincidental pass count, weakening the accuracy of the live picture.

Final full-suite run reconciled to only '12 default tests pass / 73 fail', discrepant with the long-asserted 25 and never reconciled — accounting drifted during the broken-compile period; no explicit maintained ledger (TodoWrite never used).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a coarse running failure picture, re-ran the full suite periodically, and was aware of self-inflicted regressions — clearly above anchor 5 — and notably it repeatedly and explicitly caught its own byte-diff/patching thrashing and changed tactic (a 10-level behavior). But it falls short of anchor 8's explicit, updated per-group ledger: it kept quoting an unverifiable stale '25 pass' count while the suite wouldn't compile, and the 25-vs-12 counts never reconciled, showing the live picture had drifted. That combination places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: After the first NOA test passed, the agent hit 234 failing tests but never performed byte-diff analysis on its output vs goldens; it categorized failures by guesswork and moved to bulk implementation rather than tracing any diff to a root cause in the Java model.

Repeatedly acknowledged its layout algorithms 'just return sorted nodes instead of proper algorithm' and left them wrong; abandoned components (alignment/analysis left as stubs) rather than correcting the underlying model — matches anchor 0's 'abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.'

Did recognize 'we're going in circles with mass patching / blind regex replacement is causing more harm than good' and once resolved to fix files individually — a genuine course-correction, but about its own tooling workflow, not the Java-behavior model, and it relapsed into mass patching repeatedly.

The algorithmic understanding of link interleaving was inferred from golden files up front (reverse-engineering), not derived from correcting a falsified assumption via a byte-diff, so it doesn't count toward this dimension.

Trajectory ends still firefighting compilation errors from corrupted stubs (connected_components returning f64, etc.); no evidence of any diff-driven refinement of the Java format/algorithm model in the entire back half.

dimensions.reasoning: The dimension asks whether the agent revised its model of Java behavior when a parity byte-diff falsified an assumption. The agent almost never reached that loop: it inferred the layout algorithm from goldens up front, passed a small set of basic tests, then abandoned the ~234 failing components as simplified stubs without ever diffing output against goldens or returning to the Java source to fix a general rule. Its only real course-correction was recognizing its destructive regex-patching workflow (adjacent tooling meta-work, and repeatedly relapsed), not a corrected Java-behavior model. This sits just above anchor 0 (forcing a failing approach / abandoning components) with a trace of self-awareness, well short of anchor 5's 're-read Java and adjust the approach' — placing it at 2.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Read Java FabricLink.java, SIFImportLoader.java, BioFabricNetwork.java to derive Link/Network/SIF algorithms from the reference rather than fitting to output — genuine faithful-port intent for core components.
Repeatedly read Java processLinks() to understand the exact link-ordering algorithm for the default layout, cross-referencing source rather than only goldens.

Explicitly leaned on golden-derived inference: 'reverse-engineer formats', 'exact algorithm can be inferred from golden files', 'algorithm from golden EDA analysis' — used goldens as a derivation source, a mild golden-specific assumption, though algorithmic rather than per-input.
Left other layout modes as 'simplified (just return sorted nodes)' placeholders producing incorrect output — an incomplete general port, but not hardcoded/golden-fitted.
Endgame: no evidence of stress-testing edge cases beyond provided samples or explicit reasoning about held-out generalization; treated visible byte-parity as the goal.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented general algorithms for the components it completed, drawing them from the actual Java reference (FabricLink, SIFImportLoader, processLinks) and never hardcoding or keying on specific inputs — ruling out anchors 0 and 3's core failure mode. It used goldens partly as checks and partly as an inference source ('inferred from golden files'), and never explicitly reasoned about held-out generalization or stress-tested edge cases beyond the samples, so it falls short of anchor 8. This matches anchor 5: general logic per component with goldens used as checks/derivation rather than as targets to overfit.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
